title: Ishmael
lead: Abraham's firstborn son, by Hagar, whose name means "God hears." God promised to make him a great nation with twelve princes (Genesis 17:20); his descendants are the tribes of the Arabian desert, and Islamic tradition traces the northern Arabs and Muhammad to him.

sections.b: Ishmaelite traders buy Joseph (Genesis 37:25–28; 39:1), Esau marries Ishmael's daughter (Genesis 28:9), and the twelve sons of Ishmael are listed again in Chronicles (1 Chronicles 1:28–31). Kedar and Nebaioth stand for the desert Arabs in the prophets, sometimes in judgment and sometimes in a vision of the nations bringing gifts to Zion (Isaiah 60:7; Jeremiah 49:28–29). Paul uses Ishmael, the son "born by the flesh," as a figure in his argument about the promise (Galatians 4:22–29). In the Qur'an, Isma'il is a prophet and helps Abraham build the Kaaba (Qur'an 2:127; 19:54).
